text:
ash: Quick heads-up  we launched prefetch-surge-v1 (adaptive burst + micro-prefetch) to hosted canary (20%) at 2117778888. dropping the headline numbers and rollout plan here.

deploy-bot: release ash/prefetch-surge-v1 -> canary (20%) succeeded. details: https://internal.redwood/deploys/2117778888

ash: Canary vs baseline (same traffic slice): p50 -19% (60ms -> 49ms), p99 -24% (420ms -> 320ms), token cost per req -15%. GPU busy fraction down ~9%.

leigh: Nice. Any regressions on long-context routes?

ash: Long-context (>=1500 tokens) neutral p50, occasional small p99 uptick (~3-5%) in a few routes due to batching alignment; cost benefits persist. Full breakdown on telemetry: https://internal.redwood/telemetry/prefetch-surge-canary

omar: Product: will this change model outputs or cause flakiness in generations?

ash: No model-level changes  serving-layer only. We ran eval/regression suite  no semantic diffs. If you spot issues, tag #eng-runtime.

tara: Ops: what's the rollback key and quick toggle?

ash: Runbook live. Rollback flag: runtime.prefetch_surge=false. Quick toggle:

```
redwoodctl feature set runtime.prefetch_surge=false --scope=hosted --selector=canary
```

infra: We've adjusted GPU memory and kernel-fallback alerts for the canary pool. We'll page on eviction or p99 drift.

eng-oncall: Suggest adding a short long-context smoke (2 prompts ~2k tokens) to the canary pipeline to catch edge cases before expanding.

ash: Good idea  adding 3m long-context smoke now. Plan: stay at 20% for 24h, if p99 stable expand to 50% then 100% over 48h. We'll post a 72h retro with econ tables and per-route notes. Thanks team  big props to the runtime crew (Leigh, Omar, Jin). :tada:
